protections: download_sketchfab_model pre-validates every archive member before extractall: os.path.normpath/abspath containment against abs_temp_dir plus a '..' substring check (addon.py:1847-1873), with extraction only after the loop (addon.py:1875).

Every remote download is written through a private tempfile.mkdtemp()/NamedTemporaryFile and cleaned up afterwards (addon.py:576, addon.py:672, addon.py:803, addon.py:1462, addon.py:1527, addon.py:1841, addon.py:2279, addon.py:2359).
import_generated_asset_hunyuan_ai only accepts http(s) zip URLs (addon.py:2354-2356) - a transport scheme check, not path containment.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The include keys that carry subdirectories look like ordinary legitimate paths, so a solver can dismiss the coupling and flatten them with os.path.basename, not noticing that addon.py:826 exists precisely to recreate those subdirectories for the glTF import.

file_url.split('/')[-1] cannot contain a path separator, so the derived name cannot traverse - true on POSIX but not on Windows, where a backslash-bearing last URL segment is passed straight into os.path.join and normalised as a separator.

It is the separate Hunyuan3D integration (own scene checkbox addon.py:317-323 and its own MCP tool src/blender_mcp/server.py:1100-1123), not the PolyHaven handler the advisory names; and zipfile.extractall already normalises member names, so the missing validation loop looks redundant.
A containment guard already exists here and the separate '..' substring check (addon.py:1869) catches the relative traversal case, so the missing os.sep on the prefix comparison looks cosmetic.
The caller-supplied task_uuid/request_id only becomes a path prefix; tempfile appends a random suffix, so no chosen file can be overwritten, and this is the Hyper3D integration rather than PolyHaven.

The filepath is supplied by the MCP server itself (src/blender_mcp/server.py:313-319) and the localhost socket already exposes execute_code (addon.py:280, addon.py:491-506), so there is no trust boundary for this handler to defend.

conflicts.what: The natural broad fix (os.path.basename or reject any include key containing '/') closes the traversal at addon.py:825 but destroys the legitimate nested sidecar paths whose parent directories addon.py:826 explicitly creates for the glTF import at addon.py:838.

A shared 'every written path must stay under a temp dir' helper applied uniformly would reject the absolute temp filepath the MCP server legitimately passes to get_viewport_screenshot (src/blender_mcp/server.py:313-319, addon.py:434-461).

fairness_risks: Legitimate PolyHaven include keys carry subdirectories: addon.py:826 creates the parent directory and the glTF importer at addon.py:838 resolves relative sidecar references, so basename-flattening or rejecting any '/' breaks a valid model import.
Normal zips in both importers contain nested directories; a rule that refuses any archive entry containing a separator breaks legitimate Sketchfab/Hunyuan models (addon.py:1875, addon.py:2374).

A guard wrapped only around the open() at addon.py:831 leaves os.makedirs() at addon.py:826 creating the attacker's directory outside temp_dir first; the containment check has to precede directory creation.
The MCP server supplies an absolute temp path to get_viewport_screenshot (src/blender_mcp/server.py:313-319); a global 'no absolute filepath' rule breaks screenshot capture (addon.py:434-461).

execute_blender_code is an intentional arbitrary-Python tool (src/blender_mcp/server.py:375-390, addon.py:491-506, README.md:326); any rule that treats all socket commands as untrusted input contradicts a documented feature.

A rule that rejects URLs containing '..' or backslashes outright would also refuse legitimate PolyHaven CDN URLs (addon.py:800); for T3 the check has to apply to the derived filename at addon.py:808-809, not to the URL.

The handlers must still write the main model file and the include files to disk and then import them (addon.py:815, addon.py:831, addon.py:838); 'refuse the download' is not an acceptable general fix.

design.why: Four independent fix groups: {T1,T2} at the PolyHaven include join, T3 at the URL-derived main filename, T4 at the Hunyuan extractor, T6 at the Hyper3D temp-file prefix. Each carries a different dismissal: 'the report only says traversal, so flattening is a safe fix' (T2, the mimo-type coupled value), 'split("/")[-1] cannot traverse' (T3), 'it is another integration and extractall already normalises' (T4, the deepseek-type xhard route), and 'a random suffix makes the prefix harmless' (T6, deepseek-type). That beats an advisory-only design (one easy trap, no mimo/deepseek split) and beats padding with T5/T7, which are an already-working guard and by-design socket code whose 'fixes' would contradict legitimate absolute-path use.
